clue.text: Clyde valley native, last of several to stroll round loch

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of each of the next two words, several and to
round says the stroll word goes around the letter for loch

parts.note: to stroll is to wander
L is the map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian takes a walk around a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes L and O from 'several' and 'to'; 'round' puts L inside WANDER to make WLANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clyde valley lies in the Scottish Lowlands, so someone born there is a native of that lower-lying region of Scotland.

clue.text: Liberal viewpoint reportedly providing leeway

indicators.note: reportedly says the letters for Liberal and viewpoint are only heard, not spelt as written

parts.note: L is a standard abbreviation for liberal; a viewpoint is an attitude, an outlook on something

explanation.surface: A tolerant outlook, the clue claims, gives people room to manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, L plus ATTITUDE run together; the written word drops one T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both mean freedom of action or scope to act as one chooses.

clue.text: That's amazing! It goes up and down!

definitions.note: an exclamation of astonishment, and the three letters read the same up or down the grid

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading up and reading down give the same letters, so the word reads the same both ways

parts.note: an exclamation of astonishment, and the three letters read the same up or down the grid

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a yo-yo or a lift that rises and falls.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment, said when something impresses or amazes the speaker.

clue.text: In maturity soldiers are of the same mind

indicators.note: In says the soldiers sit inside the word for maturity

parts.note: maturity is age, as in coming of age
RE, the Royal Engineers, is the usual abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Older soldiers tend to see eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: people who concur share a single opinion between them.

clue.text: Daunting day I perform, covering Prom, perhaps

indicators.note: covering says the perform word wraps around the Prom word

parts.note: to perform, as a vocalist does, is to sing
a Prom, one of the BBC Proms summer series in London, is a kind of concert

explanation.surface: A performer frets about singing at the Proms, the famous London concert season.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are the BBC's summer concert season in London; 'covering' wraps SING around CONCERT, after D and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something unsettling or unnerving puts a person off their stride.

clue.text: Course teacher set up on Bismarck

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits above the second
in a down clue, set up means the teacher word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
Otto von Bismarck was the nineteenth-century German chancellor

explanation.surface: A history teacher prepares a lesson on Bismarck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a school course but is a course of a meal; 'set up' makes RIS, and 'on' stacks it above Bismarck's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of a meal can be an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Flipping rotten fish

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over so it reads backwards

parts.note: rotten food is bad

explanation.surface: A fish that has gone off, with 'Flipping' as a mild curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads like a mild British curse, but it turns BAD around.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small European flatfish.

clue.text: Pharmacist in Norfolk town receiving writer with hesitation

indicators.note: with joins the hesitation on at the end
receiving says the town takes the writer inside it

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county
a pen is a writing implement
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A chemist in a Norfolk town takes in a hesitant author.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is an English county; 'receiving' takes the writer inside its small market town, and 'with' adds the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist makes up and hands out medicines, so is called by this title too.

clue.text: Brazen bachelor of advanced years

parts.note: someone of advanced years is old

explanation.surface: An elderly single man behaves shamelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shameless, forward, unafraid to stand out.

clue.text: In the direction of where nurses often go

definitions.meaning: hospital nurses go off to the wards, read as two words

explanation.surface: Nurses heading off to their duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning heading for; split in two it names the hospital rooms nurses walk to.

clue.text: Rope-maker extremely sceptical about savings scheme

indicators.note: about says those outer letters go around the savings scheme
extremely takes the extreme letters, the first and last, of sceptical

parts.note: an ISA, Individual Savings Account, is a British tax-free savings scheme

explanation.surface: A cynical rope manufacturer distrusts a savings plan.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account; 'about' puts it inside S and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Its strong plant fibre is twisted into cord, so the plant is what makes the rope.

clue.text: Sample part of Malta's terrain

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A visitor tries a little of Malta's landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to try a small amount, as of food or an experience.

clue.text: Perversely cause club to retain old serving vessel

indicators.note: perversely means contrarily, so the letters of cause are set in a twisted order
to retain says the club holds the letter for old inside it

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: Someone awkward gets a club to hang on to an antique dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perversely' looks like a comment on behaviour but signals an anagram of 'cause'; 'to retain' has the club hold the old letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a boat-shaped jug used at table for pouring gravy.

clue.text: Start in old-fashioned group

parts.note: something old-fashioned is out of style, out
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Beginning life in an outdated crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the beginning of an undertaking, as in 'from the very first'.

clue.text: A key choice, fostering

parts.note: D is a musical key
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: Taking in a child is presented as a key choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fostering' looks like a verb but is the noun-like definition: taking up, as an idea or a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the sense of taking up and nurturing, of a child or an idea.

clue.text: Lookalike confronted and betrayed

parts.note: a lookalike is a double
to cross someone is to confront or oppose them

explanation.surface: A spy's doppelganger is confronted and sold out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cheated by a supposed ally who worked secretly against one.

clue.text: Good fortune currently visible in siege city

parts.note: good fortune is luck
currently means now

explanation.surface: Lady luck shows up at a besieged city.
explanation.walkthrough: The city in northern India was besieged during the 1857 Indian Rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Indian city whose British residency was famously besieged in 1857.

clue.text: Sporting type erecting barrier around field

definitions.meaning: a sportsperson who duels with foils or sabres
one who builds a boundary of posts and rails round a field

explanation.surface: An athlete doing a spot of farm work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a swordsman in the sport and a person who puts up enclosures.

clue.text: Fight for a bit

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a scrappy little brawl and a leftover morsel or fragment.

clue.text: Rolling swell certain to engulf stern of brig

indicators.note: to engulf says the certain word swallows the letter taken from brig

parts.note: certain means sure

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so it takes the last letter of brig

explanation.surface: A big wave is bound to swamp the back of a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a powerful onward rush, especially of the sea.

clue.text: Turkish commander crossing river in Indian city

indicators.note: crossing says the commander goes around the river letter

parts.note: an aga was an Ottoman military commander

explanation.surface: An Ottoman officer fords a river while in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the city in Uttar Pradesh that is home to the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Express exasperation when elderly relative pinches ring

indicators.note: pinches says the relative grips the ring between her letters

parts.note: gran is a grandmother
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone sighs when Granny steals a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to let out a deep sound of annoyance or despair.

clue.text: Middle Easterner following prime minister's daughter?

indicators.note: following picks out what comes after the daughter letter in the prime minister's name

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Middle Eastern figure is the next generation after a premier's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'what follows D in DISRAELI': drop that opening D.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a citizen of a Middle Eastern state on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Italian leader supporting the Spanish priest

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the first part sits beneath the second

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Italian

explanation.surface: An Italian chief backs the Spanish cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is in answer order: EL sits above I.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Old Testament priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel.

clue.text: Take steps to perform on stage

definitions.meaning: to do something about a situation
to play a part in a play

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both doing something decisive and playing a role in the theatre.

clue.text: Like some music drama, unusually wearing, and endless?

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of wearing are set in an unusual order
endless says the word and loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Some opera is described as unusually tiring and never-ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges WEARING; 'endless' leaves AN from 'and'. The joke is that the Ring cycle is famously long and tiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner called his operas music dramas, so music of that kind belongs to his style.
